A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spectral conditional independence testing framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable. Appendices A–B can be matched across versions; v2 adds an experimental Appendix C.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic experiments measuring Type I error and power in Section 6 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic experiments, breast-cancer data analysis, and additional sensitivity, timing, and causal-query experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The core bi-level learning and partial-covariance test remain. Section 3 and Appendix A revise the empirical losses, changing the outer coefficient from -2/(m-1) to -2/m and correcting the placement of M and N. Appendix C additionally specifies test-time SVD rank pruning and adjusted chi-square calibration, absent from v1's stated testing procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only a post-nonlinear synthetic model. V2 adds a nonsmooth high-dimensional scenario, a multivariate shared-noise benchmark, TCGA-BRCA molecular/image/survival data, and conditional-independence queries on a Sachs-inspired graph. These substantially broaden the represented distributions, domain, and testing scenarios.

E2.justification: V1's Figures 2–3 display comparisons with KCI/KCIT and GCIT. V2's corresponding Figure 2 additionally evaluates RCIT, DGCIT, and NNLSCIT; its kernel comparison in Figure 5 includes GCM. Other methods merely named in v1's prose are not established as evaluated comparators. LPCIT is explicitly excluded from v2's kernel results because of runtime.

E3.justification: The main synthetic experiment changes its generating equations and stated sample size from 1500 to 1000. Its plotted conditioning-dimension range changes from 10–250 to 50–300; v1's prose inconsistently states 100–500. V2 also introduces sample-size, hyperparameter, and signal-strength sweeps, plus a fixed-sample-size timing protocol. These are substantive evaluation-design changes.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's dimensionality benchmark, v2 adds a nonsmoothness stress test against NNLSCIT, truncation-rank/learning-rate/regularization sensitivity studies, runtime comparisons, and a controlled signal-strength ablation. Appendix C also adds a small causal-query case study. These examine failure conditions, robustness, computational cost, and applicability previously untested.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 100 repetitions for their main synthetic experiments. V2 adds uncertainty bands and supplementary reporting of means and standard deviations, including ten timing repetitions. Its high-dimensional experiment has unresolved reporting inconsistencies: Appendix C specifies 500 repetitions and standard errors, whereas Figure 10's caption specifies five repetitions and standard deviations.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the initial synthetic curves under changed conditions and adds numerous experimental outcomes. Table 1 reports breast-cancer p-values below 0.001 for SpectralCIT, 0.068 for KCIT, and 0.38 for NNLSCIT; Table 6 reports powers of 1.00 and 0.75 for two causal queries. New sensitivity, timing, and robustness findings are additions, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 replaces v1's joint approximation-and-whitening error condition with a covariance-only validity error. Theorem 4.2 uses a separate approximation error and revises the separation bound, including a d log(1/delta) term. Appendix A changes Theorem A.1's assumption from Hilbert-Schmidt to compact, and Appendix B.9 revises power-bound expressions. These alter mathematical assumptions and guarantees despite largely retained proofs.

C1.justification: V2 strengthens the central validity claim by separating calibration from operator-approximation quality and emphasizing moment control and bounded activations; v1 conditions validity on joint representation consistency. The introduction also explicitly claims a novel nonsmooth benchmark and multimodal breast-cancer validation as contributions. The underlying spectral-testing objective remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of NNLSCIT's nonsmoothness failure, residual molecular prognostic information after conditioning on images, and signal strength relative to dimensionality. Its new limitations discussion acknowledges conservative calibration, possible power loss, nonstandard hyperparameter selection, and unavailable explicit learning rates. V1 lacks these experiment-specific interpretations and qualifications.

D1.justification: New Appendix C documents MLP architectures, Tanh activations, Xavier initialization, Adam, 400 epochs, warm-up steps, an 80/20 split, tuning objectives and search grids, and hardware/software. V2 also adds a code-repository link and detailed histology preprocessing. These substantially improve documentation; they do not establish that previously unspecified v1 settings were different.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes its CI-testing extension from prior spectral estimation and uncertainty-quantification work, expands discussion of regression requirements, kernel selection, and benchmarking practice, and adds substantial computational-pathology positioning. Relevant additions include He et al., Pogodin et al. (2023), Wang et al.'s kernel-selection work, and clinical studies. V1's density-ratio discussion and Sugiyama citation are removed.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the introduction's motivation, common background and method explanations, theoretical narrative, related work, and conclusion. Experiments move before related work, related-work categories are reorganized, and limitations and experimental-details sections are added. Terminology is standardized to SpectralCIT. This exceeds the structural changes required merely to insert new results.

P2.justification: The original separate error and power plots are replaced by newly plotted paired panels with revised axes, legends, and uncertainty shading. V2 adds a pathology-processing diagram, numerous experimental and sensitivity plots, a causal graph, and six tables. These substantially change the visual presentation beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's thin empirical support and missing reproducibility recipe through assumption-stress tests, controlled sensitivities, measured runtime, and detailed implementation information. Revised loss formulas also remove dimensional inconsistencies. These gains make the work substantially easier to assess and reproduce, despite unresolved shortcomings: Appendix C's pruned-statistic calibration is not reconciled with the full-statistic theorem, and Figure 10 conflicts with the text about repetitions and uncertainty.
